newsitem.title: ITALY: Sorin deal accounts for 4 pct of its sales.
newsitem.headline: Sorin deal accounts for 4 pct of its sales.

text.p: Italy's Sorin Biomedica SpA, which is controlled by Fiat, said the sales of its nuclear medicine business to Amersham International Plc accounted for about four percent of the group's total sales.

Sorin said that Amersham will be paying a minimum of 44 billion lire including royalties and assumed debts and creditors. Amersham announced the deal earlier today, and said the new business will trade as Amersham Sorin Radiofarmaci.

Sorin heads up the bio-engineering activities of chemicals holding Snia Bpd, which itself is controlled by Fiat. Fiat said in June that it had no plans to sell off Snia Bpd, but that it was open to new partners for the group.
Last year, Fiat had attempted to offload Snia Bpd and its three operating companies Snia Fibre, chemicals group Caffaro and Sorin in part of a so-called SuperGemina plan, which has now been shelved.
